title: An immersion has fibres of degree at most one (Stacks 03J9)
statement: Let $j:Z\to X$ be an immersion of schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion] (a closed immersion followed by an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]). Then the integer $1$ bounds the degrees of the fibres of $j$ [def-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-bound]: for every $x\in X$ the fibre $Z_x=Z\times_X\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$ is finite over $\kappa(x)$ with $\dim_{\kappa(x)}\Gamma(Z_x,\mathcal O_{Z_x})\le1$ (it is empty if $x\notin j(Z)$ and isomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$ over $\kappa(x)$ if $x\in j(Z)$). In particular the fibres of $j$ are universally bounded. (Stacks Project, Morphisms, Lemma Tag 03J9.)

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma Tag 03J9 (lemma-immersion-universally-bounded), line 15459, and its proof ('The integer n = 1 works')

proof.text: Base change j to Spec kappa(x). The fibre projection q is a preimmersion because j is an immersion and preimmersions are stable under base change. Spec of a field is a discrete one-point space, so the range of q is closed. Thus q is a closed immersion, by IsClosedImmersion.of_isPreimmersion; this avoids factoring the immersion into open and closed parts.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma Tag 03J9 (lemma-immersion-universally-bounded), line 15459, and its proof ('The integer n = 1 works')

proof.text: Use j.fiberHomeo x to identify the fibre with the inverse image of x. Outside the range, a point of the fibre would give a point mapping to x, a contradiction. On the range, a point z mapping to x gives a fibre point w via the inverse homeomorphism. As Spec kappa(x) has one point, q is then surjective. A surjective closed immersion into this reduced scheme is an isomorphism, by Mathlib isIso_of_isClosedImmersion_of_surjective. Algebraically, its defining ideal in the field is proper, hence zero, so the quotient map is an isomorphism.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma Tag 03J9 (lemma-immersion-universally-bounded), line 15459, and its proof ('The integer n = 1 works')

proof.text: The closed immersion q is finite by the Mathlib closed-immersion instance. In the nonempty case, finrankΓ_eq_of_iso transports its dimension to the identity of Spec kappa(x), and finrankΓ_id gives dimension one. In the empty case the global sections are subsingleton and Module.finrank_zero_of_subsingleton gives dimension zero. Therefore every fibre is finite and has degree at most one.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma Tag 03J9 (lemma-immersion-universally-bounded), line 15459, and its proof ('The integer n = 1 works')

proof.text: Combine the degree bound and the two cases, and use the integer one as the witness of HasUniversallyBoundedFibers.
